knowledge_weighting.method: entry-weighted mean of O*NET 31.0 importance (Scale IM): entry targets weight 2; other linked occupations in Job Zone 4 or 5 (or the entry targets' Job Zone) weight 1; Manager, Chief, Postsecondary-faculty, All Other, Supervisor, Director and Treasurers and Controllers titles, and non-target occupations in other Job Zones, weight 0
knowledge_weighting.note: top_knowledge/top_skills are the unweighted mean over all linked occupations (kept for comparison); the outline uses the entry-weighted lists.

skipped_knowledge.reason: management and planning knowledge matters most after several years of experience, so the outline gives it no course slot (a management elective is optional)
service and client-relations knowledge; the outline leaves it to internships, part-time work and the practice tasks rather than a course slot
office procedures and records handling; usually learned on the job, so it gets no course slot
teaching and training others is built through presenting, tutoring and peer teaching in projects rather than a dedicated course

outline_elements.rule: English Language is placed in Year 1 general education; workplace and management elements (Customer and Personal Service, Administrative, Clerical, Administration and Management, Personnel and Human Resources, Education and Training) get no course slot unless the major's CIP series is about them; the next three elements go to Year 2 and up to three more (ordered by importance to the entry targets) to Year 3; if fewer than two remain for Year 3, knowledge rated at least 2.5 for the entry targets fills it

method.supervisory_tasks: task statement matches a supervisory/managerial pattern (supervise, provide supervision, direct and coordinate, direct the work/activities/staff of, manage staff/personnel/employees/workers/teams, oversee the work/staff, hire, subordinates, assign work to, evaluate the work/performance of, train and supervise); 'under supervision' does not count

quality_flags.note: Authored tier: entry targets and practice tasks were chosen and reviewed per major, so the generated-tier plausibility flags are not applied. Informational only: cited tasks whose O*NET statement is supervisory are listed; their authored scenarios say when they are practice for a later or graduate role.

entry_target_basis: Job Zone 4 linked occupations (excluding Manager/Chief/Postsecondary/All Other/Supervisor/Director/Treasurers and Controllers titles), ranked by similarity of their O*NET knowledge-importance profile to the average profile of the eligible linked occupations (Pearson correlation), base O*NET-SOC .00 codes first

entry_target_review.note: Data Scientists, Actuaries and Business Intelligence Analysts are direct entry roles for statistics graduates.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Using a large public health dataset (for example, the CDC's behavioral risk factor survey with several hundred thousand respondents), analyze the relationship between hours of sleep and self-reported poor mental health days. Write the analysis report: how you load and subset the data, why and how you apply survey weights and design variables, handling of missing and 'don't know' responses, the model used, results presented with confidence intervals, and limitations. Cite the data source and year.

rubric.description: Uses survey weights and design variables properly for population estimates and standard errors.
Recodes special response codes and handles missing data transparently.
Interprets associations without causal claims and notes self-report and cross-sectional limits.

reference_answer_outline: Load the annual file; subset adults with valid sleep and mental health items.
Recode codes for don't know and refused to missing; define sleep categories.
Survey-weighted estimates with strata and cluster variables.
Model: survey-weighted regression with age, sex and other controls.
Limitations: cross-sectional, self-reported, possible reverse causation.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. A startup wants to sell one-year accident-and-illness pet insurance for dogs with a 250 deductible and 80 percent reimbursement up to 5,000. Using clearly invented claim data (claim frequency and average claim by age band), compute a pure premium per age band, add expense and profit loads to get a gross premium, test sensitivity to a 20 percent rise in claim frequency, and write a memo on whether the plan is financially sound, what data you would need before launch, and what regulatory review applies.

rubric.description: Pure premium equals frequency times severity after deductible and coinsurance; loads are applied correctly.
Sensitivity analysis is computed and its effect on soundness explained, including adverse selection.
Memo identifies data gaps and that rates and forms need regulatory filing and actuarial sign-off.

reference_answer_outline: Expected paid claim: frequency times (severity minus deductible) times 0.8, capped.
Gross premium equals pure premium divided by (1 minus expense and profit ratio).
Sensitivity: 20 percent frequency increase raises the loss ratio by about the same proportion.
Risks: older dogs, breed effects, anti-selection, small data.
Need credible claims data or reinsurance; state filing and qualified actuary review.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Invented ticket: the sales director says the regional revenue dashboard shows 4.2 million for last month while the finance report shows 4.6 million, and she presents to the board tomorrow. Write how you would handle the ticket: the first response to the director, a step-by-step diagnosis (filters, refresh status, definitions such as booked versus invoiced revenue, time zones, currency, returns), how you document the root cause and fix, and how you prevent this kind of mismatch in the future.

rubric.description: Acknowledges urgency, sets expectations and gives a timeline.
Checks likely causes in a sensible order and reconciles the two numbers to the source.
Documents root cause and adds definitions, reconciliation checks or data alerts.

reference_answer_outline: Reply within the hour with a plan and time of next update.
Check refresh timestamp, filters, date ranges, revenue definition, returns and currency conversion.
Reconcile both figures to the general ledger; identify the gap's components.
Fix dashboard logic or add a note; tell the director which number to use for the board and why.
Prevention: shared metric definitions, automated daily reconciliation, data freshness label.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Invented results: an online bookstore ran a three-week A/B test of free shipping over 25 versus over 35. Conversion rose from 3.1 to 3.4 percent (about 120,000 visitors per arm), average order value fell from 41 to 37, and shipping costs per order rose by 0.80. Write a one-page recommendation to the executive team: statistical significance and confidence intervals, the profit impact per 1,000 visitors under stated margin assumptions, risks such as novelty effects, and your recommendation with a follow-up plan.

rubric.description: Tests the conversion difference and reports uncertainty correctly for the stated sample sizes.
Converts results into profit per visitor with explicit margin assumptions.
Makes a decision-oriented recommendation that weighs uncertainty and proposes follow-up.

reference_answer_outline: Difference 0.3 points; standard error from both proportions; significant at the stated sample size.
Revenue per 1,000 visitors: 34 orders times 37 versus 31 orders times 41.
Profit using a margin assumption minus extra shipping cost.
Risks: novelty, seasonality, effects on repeat purchases.
Recommendation depends on profit result; follow-up test of threshold 30.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Invented data: a pension plan observed 2,000 members aged 60 to 64 for three years with total exposure of 5,700 person-years and 34 deaths, and 1,500 members aged 65 to 69 with 4,200 person-years and 52 deaths. Estimate the central death rate for each age band with a confidence interval, compare them with a published national life table (cite which one you would use) via actual-to-expected ratios, explain whether the plan's data are credible enough to use alone, and recommend how to blend plan experience with the standard table.

rubric.description: Computes rates as deaths over exposure and gives a sensible interval (e.g. Poisson-based).
Calculates actual-to-expected ratios against a cited standard table correctly.
Discusses credibility given the small number of deaths and recommends a reasoned blending approach.

reference_answer_outline: Rates about 0.0060 and 0.0124 per person-year.
Poisson interval: deaths plus or minus about 1.96 times the square root of deaths, divided by exposure.
Expected deaths from the table's rates times exposure; actual-to-expected ratios.
Limited credibility with under 100 deaths per band.
Blend with credibility weighting or apply a scaling factor to the standard table.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. A regional grocery chain's BI team delivers nightly sales dashboards, a weekly inventory report and monthly finance extracts to 300 users, and data have arrived late four times this month. Write a plan to manage the flow: map the data pipeline steps and dependencies, set delivery times and service levels for each product, define monitoring and alerting for late or failed loads, a communication process when data are late, and a monthly review of reliability metrics.

rubric.description: Maps sources, transformations and dependencies and identifies likely bottlenecks.
Each product has a delivery time, freshness indicator and owner.
Includes automated alerts, status notices to users and reliability metrics with review.

reference_answer_outline: Pipeline: point-of-sale export, warehouse load, transformations, dashboard refresh.
Service levels: dashboards by 6:00, inventory Monday 8:00, finance on business day 2.
Alerts if a job fails or runs late; on-call rotation.
User status banner and email when data are late, with estimated time.
Monthly on-time rate, incidents and root causes reviewed with stakeholders.
